done.why: I finished what I came for at turn 25, when the egg went into the case. After that I kept going and saw most of the reachable map: the dam, the drained reservoir, the river trip, the sandy cave, the falls. Then the thief chased me up the chimney, I put the emerald in the case beside the egg, and I peeked into the attic. Cave-ins blocked the remaining paths, I didn't want to try the maze without a way to mark it, and I stopped there.

about: It's a white house with an empty trophy case, and the world under it is mostly about water. The river runs through everything. A dam holds back a reservoir, and draining it opens up land that was underwater. A thin plastic boat carries you down toward a waterfall. Treasures are scattered along the way, a thief is hanging around, and cave-ins close off the rest of the underground. The egg itself is easy to get: you climb a tree and walk it home. It reads like a ghost of the old game with a few doors shut on purpose and a lot of new, wry writing.

ending.what: I put the jewel-encrusted egg (unopened) in the trophy case at turn 25, and the case listed it as part of my collection. No score or special message appeared. Later I added the emerald too.

moments.note: The egg's description warns that only deft fingers, 'and not, one suspects, entirely honest ones', could open the clasp. It was a sly nod to the thief.
The goal was done in 25 turns with no fanfare. The case just said 'Done.' I wasn't sure if more was expected of me.
The trap door slammed shut and someone barred it. Now I was locked underground.
'Bar bar ...' The Loud Room echoed my own words back, and saying 'echo' fixed it.
The river described as hurrying downstream 'as if it had heard something about the end of it'. Lovely.
I couldn't carry the wrench and screwdriver because of weight, so I had to make several trips to shuffle items around.
The way to the mirror room is blocked by a fresh cave-in with a chalked arrow pointing back. It was a gentle, in-world way of saying 'not this time'.
While still in the beached boat, 'go east' and 'go up' only answered 'Read the label for the boat's instructions' instead of telling me to get out first.
The cave-in south of the Round Room had rubble 'sorted into neat heaps by size' and grit still trickling down. A tiny mystery.
The painting in the Gallery was there when I entered and gone on the next 'look'. No message said who took it.
The chimney only takes you, your lamp and one more thing. Meanwhile the thief was stabbing me, so I had to abandon the scarab and the sack.
The sack wouldn't hold the scarab and emerald because the lunch and garlic filled it. I learned that under attack.

wished: I wished I could have opened the egg myself, or at least gotten some reaction when it went into the case.
I wished for a way through the cave-ins: the mirror passage past Atlantis, and the Round Room's blocked exits.
I wished I could talk to or bargain with the thief instead of just running from him.
I wished the boat told me to get out first when I tried to walk while it sat on the shore.
I wished for a way to carry the platinum bar, trunk and trident home. With the trap door barred, the chimney's one-item limit left them stranded.

lines.line: The clasp is jeweller's work, and would take a professional's fingers to undo without harm: deft fingers, and not, one suspects, entirely honest ones.
lines.why: It hinted that the thief was the one who could open it, and it was funny.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: The trophy case had a personality, and it framed what I was there to do.

lines.line: The Frigid River is wide and grey and very cold, and in a hurry, going downstream as if it had heard something about the end of it and wanted to see for itself.
lines.why: It was the best sentence in the game, and it foreshadowed the falls.

lines.line: It is dark, and has the patient look of something waiting to be told it may begin.
lines.why: The green bubble told me the panel needed something first, and it said so with charm.

lines.line: somebody has chalked an arrow on the rubble pointing back the way you came. You take the hint.
lines.why: It closed off part of the map gracefully without breaking the fiction.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: This rule decided what I could save from the thief.

fun.why: The goal itself was quick (turns 5-25). The real fun came from the dam and river chain: fixing the echo at turn 40, turning the bolt and draining the reservoir (turns 74-84), riding the boat and finding the emerald in the buoy (turns 135-137). The chimney escape from the thief was tense (turns 169-178).

engagement.why: I kept wanting to see what was around the next bend. The cave-ins with odd details (turns 90, 151) and the vanishing painting (turn 167) pulled me along. Shuffling my inventory around the weight limit dragged at times (turns 58-69).

difficulty.why: The stated goal was just climbing a tree and walking back: egg in hand at turn 8, in the case at turn 25. The optional parts were harder: weight limits, the boat, the chimney limit, and the thief at turns 169-176.

interestingness.why: The original game has been reworked in interesting ways. The egg description hints at the thief, the cave-ins close the map in-world, and the chimney has its own carrying rule. The confusing moments, like the painting vanishing at turn 167, still felt like part of the world.

prose.why: The new lines are excellent: the river 'in a hurry' (46), the bubble 'waiting to be told it may begin' (53), the trophy case's 'patient air' (23), the trident 'made for someone who expected to be obeyed by the sea' (91). They sit comfortably alongside the classic text.
